messages:
liam-customer: Hi — we're seeing intermittent JSON parse failures when using structured/json mode with streaming. Downstream parser gets 'Unexpected end of JSON input' or 'Unterminated string'. Seems correlated with user text that contains Windows paths like C:\\Users\\alex\\notes.txt. Happening ~0.5% of requests. Using redwood/text-1, stream=true, json_mode=structured. Any ideas?

maria-support: Thanks for the report, liam. Can you paste a minimal curl request and the exact raw response you get? Also which SDK/version and any proxies (ALB, CDN) between you and our endpoint?

liam-customer: Minimal repro (we're streaming with chunked transfer):
```bash
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\
  -d '{"model":"redwood/text-1","stream":true,"json_mode":"structured","input":"Open C:\\\\\\Users\\\\alex\\\\notes.txt\\nPlease summarise"}' \\
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
Raw response snippets (captured client-side):
- chunk 1 ends with: "..., \"file_path\": \"C:\\Users\\alex\"\n"\n- chunk 2 starts with: "notes.txt\\n\" , \"summary\": \"...\""
If you join them naively the chunks create an invalid escape (split escape sequence) and JSON parse fails with: `JSONError: Unterminated string at position 120`.

maria-support: Ack. Escalating to eng, asking for request-id headers and a HAR if possible.

liam-customer: request-id: req_0a1b2c3d, captured HAR attached to ticket. We do have an ALB in front, but it appears to be transparently passing bytes.

chris-engineering: Looking now. @maria-support @liam-customer can you confirm whether the chunk boundary is dropping a backslash at the end of a chunk? This sounds like the serializer sometimes splits in the middle of an escape sequence (e.g., a single backslash at the end of a chunk). If the client reassembles chunks as text and then parses, an orphaned backslash will break JSON parsing. Any raw byte captures would help.

liam-customer: I captured two chunks raw — hex dump shows chunk1 ends with 5C (\u005C, a backslash) and chunk2 begins with 6E 22 (n double-quote) which looks like the tail of a \n escape + closing quote. So the stream sent: "...\\" then next chunk brought "n\"..." — reassembly produced a backslash-newline sequence that the JSON parser didn't accept because the backslash was orphaned by the chunk boundary during incremental parse.

jenna-qa: I can repro with our internal streaming harness. Repro steps: send an input containing both backslashes and explicit \n sequences, enable streaming and a low chunk size. Reproduction occurs when serializer breaks mid-escape. Quick notes:
- This manifests on incremental parsers that parse chunks as they arrive (common in JS).
- We also saw similar failures with unicode escapes when surrogates were split.
Potential mitigations: pre-escape backslashes (replace \\ with \\\\\\ in client-sent prompt) or disable stream (stream=false) to get full document in one piece. Longer-term: avoid splitting inside escape sequences on the server serializer.

chris-engineering: Filed internal ticket INF-2026 (P2) and assigned to streaming-serializer team. Proposed short-term patch: if a chunk ends with a single backslash byte (0x5C), append an extra backslash to the chunk so the client sees an escaped backslash instead of an orphan. We'll add unit tests for escape-boundary cases and unicode surrogate pair splits. ETA: target MR tomorrow, roll-forward next day if tests pass.

maria-support: Shared the workaround with liam: either pre-escape backslashes on input, or set stream=false. Asked if they'd like a platform-level temporary toggle — they said pre-escaping is fine for now. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: deploy v3.4.2 started 2026-03-16T22:15:00Z (note: unrelated deploy, posting for context).

chris-engineering: Also adding tests for chunk-size fuzzing against invalid UTF-8 and surrogate pairs. Will post a follow-up when INF-2026 has a patch.

liam-customer: Thanks everyone — we'll implement pre-escaping of backslashes as a temporary fix and monitor. Please ping when the server-side fix lands so we can revert the client workaround.

maria-support: Thanks, closing the support loop for now; keep the ticket open for the engineering fix and update INF-2026/req_0a1b2c3d.
